  THIRD SEMESTER B.TECH. DEGREE EXAMINATIONS - NOVEMBER 2025  
  Digital System Design and Computer Organization [ECM_2122]  
Marks: 50                                                                                                         Duration: 180 mins.  
  
  PART-A  
Answer all the questions.  
  
1)                Implement the following Boolean functions using PAL with four inputs and 3-wide AND-OR structure           (4)  
  $$F1 (A, B, C, D) = Σm (7, 8, 9, 10, 11, 12, 13, 14, 15)$$  
  $$A)           F2 (A, B, C, D) = Σm (1, 2, 8, 12, 13)$$  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO1" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
  B)           Implement a mod-12 ripple up-counter using negative edge triggered JK flipflops and draw the output        (3)  
  timing diagrams.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO2" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
  C)           Write a Verilog structural code to implement 4:1 multiplexer using instances of 2:1 multiplexers in        (3)  
  dataflow.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
2)                Design a 3-bit self-correcting synchronous counter using JK flip-flops that follows the sequence 0-1-2-4   (5)  
  repeatedly, ensuring that any unused states automatically go to the 0-state on the next clock pulse.  
  A)  
  Course Outcome: "CO2" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
  B)           What is the role of Cache in computer memory organization? If a cache has 95% hit ratio, an access         (3)  
  time of 100 ns on a cache-hit, and an access time of 800 ns on a cache-miss, compute the effective  
  access time.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO5" / Cognitive Level: "Understand"  
  
  C)           Differentiate between hardware description language (such as Verilog) and C language.                      (2)  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Understand"  
  
3)                Design a Mealy synchronous sequential circuit using D flip-flops that will function as prescribed by the   (5)  
  state diagram shown below.  
  A)

Course Outcome: "CO2" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
  B)           Illustrate the use of Booth's algorithm to multiply -11 (multiplicand) and +8 (multiplier), where each     (3)  
  number is represented using 5 bits.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO5" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
  C)           Write a switch-level Verilog code for CMOS inverter using NMOS and PMOS primitives.                        (2)  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
4)        Analyze the synchronous sequential circuit shown below and obtain its state table and state diagram.                       (4)

  Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
  C)           What are the different hazards in pipelining? Explain them with an example for each.                       (2)  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO5" / Cognitive Level: "Understand"  
  
5)                Write the Verilog code in behavioral modeling to implement a 3-bit synchronous binary counter using        (4)  
  negative edge-triggered T flip-flops.  
  A)
